pk.context: 1 mg oral, steady state, healthy adults

tell: A deoxyguanosine analogue whose 1 mg tablet is pink and triangular, and is mostly cleared unchanged by the kidney.

clues.text: Tablet bioavailability is 100% relative to solution; a high-fat meal reduces exposure by 18-20%. Only about 13% binds serum proteins, and the kidney eliminates 62-73% unchanged.
The active moiety has a molecular weight of 277.28. It is a powder that is slightly soluble in water, at 2.4 mg/mL.
Approved under an NDA as 0.5 mg and 1 mg tablets and a 0.05 mg/mL oral solution, dosed once daily.
A boxed warning covers severe acute exacerbations after stopping therapy and lactic acidosis. No contraindications; headache, fatigue, dizziness and nausea are the common reactions.
Chronic hepatitis B virus infection with evidence of active viral replication, in adults and in children 2 years and older.
Its triphosphate form competes with deoxyguanosine triphosphate to block all three activities of the HBV reverse transcriptase, and weakly inhibits cellular DNA polymerases.
The generic name begins with E and has nine letters.
